verdict.rationale: Slack's own Workflow Builder is documented as a no-code way to build workflows inside Slack from a limited set of steps and triggers. The docs also cover webhook triggers that start a workflow from outside Slack, and conditional branching. The evidence does not name schedule-based or form-submission triggers, and the in-Slack event triggers it shows come only from the developer-facing Events API, which is not no-code. Missing for 10: documented scheduled triggers, form-submission triggers, no-code in-Slack event triggers (e.g. reactions or channel joins), and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a team-admin, I can build no-code workflows triggered by events, schedules, or form submissions inside the chat tool

citations.quote: Workflow Builder is a no-code way to build workflows, right in Slack. Any user can combine a limited set of steps and triggers to quickly set up an automation.
Webhook triggers for workflows - How to start a workflow from outside of Slack.
Add a branch to a workflow - How to add conditional branching that will present users with different options based on their interaction with the workflow.
Create time-saving automations in a few clicks
